notation.slot_rule: slot index follows WALK order: opener_0 is the walk-first opener
notation.T_X: orb(entry(closer_X))  - the lock target orbit of opener_X
notation.Q_X: orb(entry(opener_X))  - the repeat orbit charged by a free closer_X
notation.T_ne_Q: T_X != Q_X always (distinct words of one hexagon lie in distinct orbits)

repeat_orbit.be2: two repeat events; Q_0 and Q_1 are NOT assumed distinct

theorem_132_1.name: Theorem 132.1
theorem_132_1.statement: in every type-B (4,2) subcase the later opener's locality lock holds unconditionally
theorem_132_1.consequence: a branch where T_1 equals a known repeat orbit is EMPTY - the engine may PRUNE there instead of merely dropping the lock

lock_table.opener0_lock: UNCONDITIONAL (T_0 != Q_0 and Q_0 is the only repeat orbit)
CONDITIONAL: may break only if T_0 = Q_1, which cannot be decided when opener_1 is still unplaced

coincidence.note: the coincidence T_0 = Q_1 is possible for every split b_0 and pins entry(opener_1) into a 5-word orbit minus the 1 word shared with opener_0's hexagon - a 4/720 fraction of placements, so the beta branch is a genuinely narrow class, not an empty one

be1.note: four order types, one per |U| in {1,2,3,4}

be2.extra: opener_1 is the LAST pass of the repeat run opened by closer_0, so orb(entry(opener_1)) = Q_0

alpha.name: alpha chain
alpha.shape: opener_0 < closer_0 = opener_0 + 5 < opener_1 < closer_1 = opener_1 + 5
alpha.gap: closer_0 < opener_1 is strict; the passes between are all full

beta.name: beta nest
beta.shape: opener_0 < opener_1 = opener_0 + |U| < closer_1 = opener_1 + 5 < closer_0 = opener_0 + 10
beta.extra: Q_1 is FULL (all 5 slots used, deficit 0); closer_0 is the last pass of V

models.e_definition: e = r - O = sum over orbits of (#runs - 1); one orbit with three runs contributes 2, so Model T is legal by definition

model_T.shape: opener_0 ends the first run F; the repeat run R opened by closer_0 ends at opener_1; the repeat run R' opened by closer_1 is the third
ruled_out: opener_0 ends R' and opener_1 ends R
opener_0 ends R' and opener_1 ends F

audit.lock0mode_2: apply the lock unless a KNOWN repeat orbit equals the target
audit.lock0mode_1: alpha - assume opener_0's lock holds and apply it
audit.lock0mode_0: beta - do not apply it and REQUIRE orb(entry(opener1)) == Q(opener0)

mapping.alpha: covers Model T and Model D-alpha

findings: alpha/beta is exhaustive and sound but NOT minimal: Model T sits inside alpha with a strong positive orbit constraint that alpha does not use
the 'risky' case for opener_1 is EMPTY by Theorem 132.1, so the engine should prune there instead of dropping the lock
no third structural case is hidden: T, D-alpha, D-beta0 exhaust B/e=2 and D-beta1 is impossible

budget.note: the accounting closes exactly for every e; no one-unit overflow is derivable at this level of counting (honest negative result)

run_counts.be1_round131_reason: 25 split shapes x (P0 needs 1 branch: both opener locks unconditional; P1 needs 2: opener_0's lock is undecidable at lock time, so alpha/beta)
run_counts.be1_round132_note: the count is unchanged, but P0's opener_1 lock is now PROVED unconditional (Theorem 132.1) and beta gains the full order nest
run_counts.be2_round132_note: the alpha branch splits into Model T (positive orbit constraint) and Model D-alpha (negative one); D-beta0 is the old beta; D-beta1 is analytically dead
run_counts.split_shape_note: no proved grouping of the 25 ordered (b_0, b_1) shapes: the order and orbit theorems are stated for arbitrary b and do not depend on coarse features, so all 25 survive

exchange.hg_reason: slot index is defined by walk order, so relabelling h and g does not move any walk; 'which slot owns the free closer' is a walk invariant
exchange.verdict: RETAIN BOTH B/e=1 patterns - no proved quotient
